topics.name: Place Value
objectives: Recognise the place value of each digit in a 4-digit number (thousands, hundreds, tens and ones)
Order and compare numbers beyond 1000
Identify, represent and estimate numbers using different representations
Round any number to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000
Read Roman numerals to 100 (I to C)
Read, write, order and compare numbers to at least 1 000 000
Round any number up to 1 000 000 to the nearest 10, 100, 1000, 10 000 and 100 000
Read, write, order and compare numbers up to 10 000 000
Use negative numbers in context and calculate intervals across zero

keyVocab.definition: 1000 units grouped together
10 groups of 1000
100 groups of 1000
1000 groups of 1000
Approximate a number to the nearest 10, 100, etc.
A number less than zero
Letters used to represent numbers in the Roman system

masteryIndicators: I can explain the value of each digit in a large number
I can round numbers to any given power of 10
I can order and compare numbers in the millions
I can solve problems involving negative numbers
topics.starter: Show a large number on the board — pupils write its value on mini-whiteboards and round it to different powers of 10
topics.guidedPractice: Place value chart: teacher models partitioning 347,892; pupils identify each digit's value
topics.independentPractice: Developing: order 5 numbers up to 10,000. Expected: round numbers to 1000 and 10,000. Mastery: explain why two numbers round to the same value; create place value puzzles.
topics.masteryCheck: Write 3,045,720 in words. Round it to the nearest 1,000 and 100,000.

topics.name: Written Addition and Subtraction
objectives: Add and subtract numbers with up to 4 digits using the formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction where appropriate
Estimate and use inverse operations to check answers to a calculation
Solve addition and subtraction two-step problems in contexts

keyVocab.definition: A written method for calculating with digits aligned in columns
Moving value between columns when a digit exceeds 9
The opposite operation, used to check answers
An approximate answer calculated before solving precisely

masteryIndicators: I can add and subtract 4-digit numbers using column method with regrouping
I can use inverse to check my answer
I can solve two-step word problems
I can explain what an estimate shows
topics.guidedPractice: Teacher works through a column addition with regrouping step by step; pupils copy and then try next example
topics.independentPractice: Developing: additions without regrouping. Expected: 4-digit ± with regrouping. Mastery: two-step problems; write own problems.
topics.masteryCheck: Calculate 4,726 + 1,895. Check using the inverse. Explain your method.

topics.name: Multiplication and Division
objectives: Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12 multiplication tables
Multiply 2-digit and 3-digit numbers by a 1-digit number using formal written layout
Multiply numbers up to 4 digits by a 1- or 2-digit number using a formal written method
Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a 1-digit number using the formal written method of short division
Multiply and divide whole numbers and decimals by 10, 100 and 1000
Identify common factors, common multiples and prime numbers
Multiply multi-digit numbers up to 4 digits by a 2-digit whole number using the formal written method of long multiplication
Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a 2-digit whole number using the formal written method of long division

keyVocab.definition: A number that divides exactly into another
The result of multiplying a number by a whole number
A number with exactly two factors: 1 and itself
A written method for division by a single digit
A written method for multiplying by a 2-digit number
What is left over after division

masteryIndicators: I can recall all multiplication and division facts to 12×12
I can multiply 4-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers
I can use long division accurately
I can find all factor pairs of a number
I can explain what makes a prime number
topics.starter: Times table test: 10 questions from selected tables
topics.guidedPractice: Model long multiplication step by step with place value emphasis
topics.independentPractice: Developing: 2-digit × 1-digit. Expected: 3/4-digit × 2-digit long multiplication. Mastery: prime factor decomposition; explain why a method works.
topics.masteryCheck: Calculate 347 × 26. List all factors of 36. Is 51 prime? Explain.

topics.name: Fractions
objectives: Recognise and show, using diagrams, families of common equivalent fractions
Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator
Compare and order fractions whose denominators are all multiples of the same number
Add and subtract fractions with different denominators using the concept of equivalent fractions
Multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers
Divide proper fractions by whole numbers

keyVocab.definition: Fractions that have the same value
To reduce a fraction to its simplest form
A whole number and a fraction combined
A fraction where the numerator is greater than the denominator
A shared denominator that allows fractions to be compared or added

masteryIndicators: I can find equivalent fractions using multiplication and division
I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators
I can convert between mixed numbers and improper fractions
I can multiply a fraction by a whole number
topics.starter: Fraction wall display — which fractions are equivalent?
topics.guidedPractice: Teacher demonstrates finding common denominators to add 1/3 + 1/4; step-by-step with diagrams
topics.independentPractice: Developing: add/subtract fractions same denominator. Expected: different denominators. Mastery: multi-step fraction problems.
topics.masteryCheck: Calculate 2/3 + 3/4. Convert 11/4 to a mixed number.

topics.name: Decimals and Percentages
objectives: Recognise and write decimal equivalents to 1/4, 1/2, 3/4
Identify the value of each digit in numbers given to three decimal places
Solve problems involving numbers up to three decimal places
Recognise the per cent symbol (%) and understand that per cent relates to 'number of parts per hundred'
Recall and use equivalences between simple fractions, decimals and percentages

keyVocab.definition: A number with digits after the decimal point representing parts of a whole
The dot separating whole numbers from fractional parts
A number expressed as a fraction of 100
Parts of one whole divided into 10 equal pieces
Parts of one whole divided into 100 equal pieces
Parts of one whole divided into 1000 equal pieces

masteryIndicators: I can convert between fractions, decimals and percentages
I can compare and order decimals to 3 decimal places
I can calculate percentages of amounts
I can solve problems using FDP interchangeably
topics.starter: FDP triangle: fill in missing fraction, decimal or percentage
topics.guidedPractice: Number line: place 0.5, 0.25, 0.75, 50%, 25%; show how fractions, decimals and percentages relate
topics.independentPractice: Developing: match equivalent FDP cards. Expected: convert and calculate percentages of amounts. Mastery: problem solving with FDP in real-world contexts.
topics.masteryCheck: Write 35% as a fraction and decimal. Find 15% of 80.

topics.name: Ratio and Proportion
objectives: Solve problems involving the relative sizes of two quantities where missing values can be found using multiplication and division facts
Solve problems involving the calculation of percentages
Solve problems involving similar shapes where the scale factor is known
Solve problems involving unequal sharing and grouping using knowledge of fractions and multiples

keyVocab.definition: A comparison of two quantities showing how many times one is as big as the other
A part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole
The number by which a shape is enlarged or reduced
Sharing in a given ratio

masteryIndicators: I can share in a given ratio
I can use ratio notation correctly
I can scale recipes and quantities
I can solve proportion problems in context
topics.starter: Recipe challenge: if this serves 4, what quantities for 6?
topics.guidedPractice: Bar model approach to ratio: 3:5 sharing 40 items
topics.independentPractice: Developing: simple 1:n ratios. Expected: sharing in 2-part ratio. Mastery: multi-step ratio and proportion problems.
topics.masteryCheck: Share £48 in the ratio 3:5. A recipe for 4 serves needs 200g flour. How much for 10?

topics.name: Algebra
objectives: Use simple formulae
Generate and describe linear number sequences
Express missing number problems algebraically
Find pairs of numbers that satisfy an equation with two unknowns
Enumerate possibilities of combinations of two variables

keyVocab.definition: A letter that represents an unknown number
A rule written with mathematical symbols
A combination of numbers, variables and operations
A mathematical statement with an equals sign showing two expressions are equal
A sequence where the difference between consecutive terms is constant

masteryIndicators: I can substitute values into a formula
I can generate sequences using algebraic rules
I can solve one-step equations
I can find all possible solutions for a two-variable equation
topics.starter: What's the rule? Give 3 terms of a sequence — pupils find and explain the rule
topics.guidedPractice: Model using balance scales to show equations; solve n + 5 = 12 with bar models
topics.independentPractice: Developing: missing number problems. Expected: one-step equations and sequences. Mastery: two-variable equations; enumerate all possibilities.
topics.masteryCheck: Find the value of n: 3n + 2 = 17. Generate the first 5 terms of the rule 2n + 1.

topics.name: Angles
objectives: Recognise angles as a property of shape and associate angles with turning
Identify right angles and know that two right angles make a half-turn
Identify acute and obtuse angles
Estimate and compare acute, obtuse and reflex angles
Know angles are measured in degrees
Identify angles at a point, angles at a point on a straight line and recognise when angles sum to 90°, 180°, 360°

keyVocab.definition: The amount of turn between two lines from a shared point
The unit used to measure angles
An angle of exactly 90°
An angle less than 90°
An angle greater than 90° but less than 180°
An angle greater than 180°

masteryIndicators: I can identify and classify angles
I can use a protractor to measure angles accurately
I can calculate missing angles on a straight line and at a point
I can explain the angle properties of triangles and quadrilaterals
topics.starter: Angle aerobics: pupils use arms to show acute, obtuse, right, reflex angles
topics.guidedPractice: Using a protractor: model measuring two angles, then pupils measure 3 given angles
topics.independentPractice: Developing: identify and name angles. Expected: measure with protractor. Mastery: calculate missing angles using properties.
topics.masteryCheck: Measure this angle. Calculate the missing angle on a straight line where one angle is 53°.

topics.name: Data Handling and Graphs
objectives: Interpret and present data using bar charts, pictograms and tables
Interpret and construct pie charts and line graphs
Solve comparison, sum and difference problems using information presented in charts
Calculate and interpret the mean as an average

keyVocab.definition: Information collected for analysis
How often something occurs
The sum of all values divided by the number of values
The value that appears most often
The middle value when data is ordered
The difference between the highest and lowest values

masteryIndicators: I can construct and interpret a bar chart
I can calculate the mean of a set of data
I can read and interpret a line graph
I can compare data sets and draw conclusions
topics.starter: Show a bar chart on the board — quick questions about data interpretation
topics.guidedPractice: Collect class data (e.g. favourite sports) and draw a bar chart together
topics.independentPractice: Developing: read given graphs. Expected: draw and label bar chart from data. Mastery: calculate mean; interpret and compare two data sets.
topics.masteryCheck: What is the mean of: 7, 4, 9, 2, 8? Describe what this tells you about the data.
